mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has stabilized at -32.9% (week t-0w), showing no further deterioration. This plateau signals that commuting constraints have reached a steady state, allowing retail-recreation demand to recover incrementally as workers resume hybrid or full schedules over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT declined from -35.6% to -32.9% over four weeks, showing stabilization
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or TRANSIT falls below -35% in any of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has declined sharply from -16.9% to -31.1% (t-3w to t-1w), then partially recovered to -23.4% (t-0w). This reversal signals a shift in outdoor recreation preferences away from parks toward retail-recreation venues, driving higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS recovered 7.7 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS continues to decline or remains below -25% for all four weeks ahead, or RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the prior four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized near -21.9% across the last two weeks, indicating a floor in remote work adoption. Combined with TRANSIT stabilization at -32.9%, this dual plateau removes barriers to retail-recreation resumption, producing a positive shift in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain within ±2 percentage points of their t-0w values
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES unchanged at -21.9% from t-1w to t-0w
fact:TRANSIT improved 2.1 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT deteriorates by more than 3 percentage points in any single week ahead, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has remained tightly constrained between -4.3% and -7.4%, indicating persistent restrictions on non-essential retail. If GROCERY_PHARM rises above -3% within the next week, it signals policy relaxation that will cascade to RETAIL_REC within two weeks, producing a positive direction.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -3% in any single week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM range is -7.4% to -4.3% over four weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM does not rise above -3% within the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines relative to the prior four-week mean despite GROCERY_PHARM improvement.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 12.7% (t-2w) to 10.9% (t-0w), indicating a gradual return to out-of-home activity. This trend will accelerate over the next four weeks as confidence in mobility safety increases, driving RETAIL_REC higher as people resume shopping and recreation routines.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 10% in any week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 1.8 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rises above 12% in any week ahead, or RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the prior four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown a consistent upward trend from -30.7% (t-1w) to -26.9% (t-0w), a 3.8-point improvement. If this linear recovery continues at the same rate, RETAIL_REC will reach approximately -22% by week t+4w, representing a positive direction relative to the prior four-week mean of -28.975%.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 3.8 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines in more than two of the next four weeks, or the four-week mean ahead is lower than -28.975%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES have both stabilized, but RETAIL_REC remains 26.9% below baseline. If TRANSIT improves by more than 3 percentage points AND WORKPLACES simultaneously rises by more than 2 percentage points within the next week, this dual signal indicates rapid reopening that will drive RETAIL_REC recovery over the following three weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves >3 points AND WORKPLACES improves >2 points in the same week
failure_condition: The dual trigger condition does not occur within the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS decline from -16.9% to -31.1% followed by recovery to -23.4% indicates volatile outdoor recreation demand. If PARKS stabilizes above -20% while RETAIL_REC remains below -25%, consumers will substitute toward indoor retail-recreation venues, producing a positive RETAIL_REC direction over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stabilizes between -20% and -15% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS volatility range is 15.2 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: PARKS does not stabilize in the -20% to -15% range for two consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the prior 28-day mean.
